title: AttAcc! Unleashing the Power of PIM for Batched Transformer-based Generative Model Inference
problem: Conventional GPU systems cannot efficiently execute attention layers in transformer-based generative models during inference, even with batching, due to various architectural constraints. The generation stage dominated by attention and fully-connected layers becomes the execution time bottleneck.
motivation: Transformer-based generative models demand immense computational and memory resources, making efficient inference critical for practical deployment at scale.
method: AttAcc builds a processing-in-memory (PIM) architecture—computation placed directly in the memory system to reduce data travel delays. The system pairs PIM with a GPU: PIM handles attention layers (the calculation steps requiring massive data reads) by leveraging high memory bandwidth, while the GPU executes fully-connected layers where raw computing power matters most. System-level optimizations coordinate the two components to accelerate batched transformer inference end-to-end.
key_novelty: AttAcc splits transformer inference between specialized memory-compute hardware for memory-hungry attention layers and GPUs for compute-heavy fully-connected layers, matching each type of work to the hardware built for it.
contributions: AttAcc: a PIM architecture optimized for efficient attention layer execution in transformer models
Heterogeneous GPU-PIM system architecture with strategic workload distribution for end-to-end TbGM inference
System-level optimizations coordinating GPU and PIM for memory bandwidth and compute exploitation
2.81x performance and 2.67x energy efficiency improvements on 175B model inference
primary_theme: PIM acceleration for transformer attention layers
